sources.title: 14.382 Spring 2017 Lecture 1: Least Squares, Adaptive Partialling Out, Simultaneous Inference
sources.supports: Population linear projection, orthogonality and rank; sample normal equations; population/sample partial regression; predictive versus causal interpretation; score-based sandwich representation.
sources.limits: Growing-dimension asymptotics are stated with unspecified regularity and without the full proof. They cannot certify the chapter's theorem assumptions.
sources.transcription_cautions: The p.4 argmin displays omit a square; derive the squared-loss objective independently. The p.3 randomization sentence says independence from X although X includes D: use a properly stated potential-outcome/baseline-covariate condition, not that literal sentence. No source empirical example or exercise will be reused.

sources.authors: A. Colin Cameron and Douglas L. Miller
sources.title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
sources.source_date: 2015, Journal of Human Resources 50(2), 317-372 in this 56-page author-hosted PDF
sources.text_inspected: II.A printed p.320; II.C-D pp.323-325, equations (7)-(16); VI opening and VI.A pp.340-341.
sources.supports: Conditional covariance and cluster-score sandwich; averaging over independent clusters; known-covariance GLS versus estimated weighting; covariance-model-dependent efficiency; robust inference with a working covariance; few-cluster bias and critical-value limitations.
sources.limits: No universal adequate cluster count or exact general t(G-1) result follows. Current software behavior, multiway methods and bootstrap refinements were not audited.
sources.equation_check: Rendered pp.324-325 confirm that the correction c multiplies the covariance, equivalently residuals are scaled by sqrt(c); text extraction dropped the square root. FGLS residuals and both weighting factors in equation (15) were checked visually.

sources.title: 14.382 Spring 2017 Lecture 4: Euler Equations, Nonlinear GMM, and Other Adventures
sources.text_inspected: Printed/PDF p.10, Lemma 2 and the immediately following long-run covariance and Newey-West estimator; reference [14] on p.22.
sources.supports: Long-run covariance as the sum of score autocovariances; Bartlett weights 1-lag/(L+1), common denominator n and symmetric lag terms; explicit dependence and moment assumptions for a stated CLT.
sources.limits: The mixing CLT is invoked, not proved there. The page asserts positive semidefiniteness but supplies neither its proof nor bandwidth conditions proving HAC consistency. General GMM results elsewhere in the PDF are outside this inspection and this preparation scope.

unavailable_lead.observed: Web retrieval failed; the papers/t0055.pdf response reported HTTP 403. The body was not inspected and access was not bypassed.

proposed_chapter_design: Begin with an original finite distribution where the best linear predictor exists but has no stipulated causal interpretation; derive the population objective and sample projection separately.

Use a small full-rank fixed design with declared positive-definite covariance to derive OLS covariance, whitening and the GLS efficiency comparison. Then perturb the working covariance while retaining the true covariance for an independent variance calculation.

Develop the IID fixed-dimension sandwich before aggregating observations into independent bounded-size clusters. Compare individual score squares with squared cluster score sums in one original example.

Use a small explicit serial-dependence process to distinguish score autocorrelation from heteroskedasticity. Derive Bartlett positive semidefiniteness from zero-extended moving sums, and label lag choice and finite-sample sensitivity.

Make finite-sample concerns substantive: rank deficiency, leverage, too few independent clusters, nonpositive estimated variances under an inappropriate truncation, and the difference between changing an estimator and changing its standard error.

Reserve at least three worked cases and ten fully solved exercises, including full-rank/GLS and sandwich proofs, one dependence transfer, and a critique of causal or exact-inference overclaiming. Numerical source examples are not a problem bank.
proof_contract_to_resolve_before_authori: Confirm what v12-c01 proves about vector LLN/CLT, continuous mapping, Slutsky, stochastic orders and matrix inversion. No growing-dimension or dependent-data theorem should be inherited by implication.

For exact fixed-design OLS/GLS results require full column rank, conditional mean zero and known positive-definite covariance; show the covariance difference is positive semidefinite. Exact Gaussian t/F inference requires its own distributional derivation.

For IID HC consistency give explicit fixed-dimension moment and nonsingular population-Gram assumptions and bound the residual-replacement error. HC1/HC2/HC3 finite-sample adjustments are not automatically exact inference.

For estimated weights, specify a finite-dimensional covariance model and a stable weighted-Gram/score limit. Consistency of an ever-growing estimated covariance array is not a complete FGLS proof condition.

For clustering, start with independent identically distributed bounded-size clusters and prove the cluster-level LLN/CLT route. Growing, unbalanced or dominant clusters require additional hypotheses; a large observation count alone is insufficient.

For HAC, either prove a deliberately bounded dependence case, including the needed CLT and residual/bandwidth errors, or label a precisely stated general theorem as invoked after retrieving its proof source. Positive semidefiniteness alone proves neither consistency nor coverage.

Keep inference and identification separate. A changed weighting rule can change a projection estimand under mean misspecification; robust standard errors do not supply exogeneity or causal identification.
